mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate signals monetary easing, which lowers borrowing costs and increases consumer and business spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in >40% of cases where FEDFUNDS declines, or if the Rank IC is below 0.03 in walk-forward analysis.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate indicates a strong labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in >40% of cases where UNRATE declines, or if the Rank IC is below 0.03 in walk-forward analysis.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) reflects strong demand in the housing market, which spills over into broader economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in >40% of cases where HOUST increases, or if the Rank IC is below 0.03 in walk-forward analysis.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strong supply-side activity, which supports economic growth and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in >40% of cases where INDPRO increases, or if the Rank IC is below 0.03 in walk-forward analysis.

mechanism_narrative: When both GDP (GDPC1) and real personal consumption expenditure (RSAFS) increase, it signals strong aggregate demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in >40% of cases where both GDPC1 and RSAFS increase, or if the Rank IC is below 0.03 in walk-forward analysis.

mechanism_narrative: A high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%) indicates tight monetary conditions, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in >40% of cases where FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or if the Rank IC is below 0.03 in walk-forward analysis.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is low and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is high, it indicates a tight labor market with potential wage inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as margins get squeezed.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in >40% of cases where UNRATE is low and FEDFUNDS is high, or if the Rank IC is below 0.03 in walk-forward analysis.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases while real personal consumption expenditure (RSAFS) decreases, it indicates an imbalanced economic expansion that may lead to negative S&P 500 returns as growth becomes unsustainable.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in >50% of cases where PAYEMS increases and RSAFS decreases, or if the Rank IC is above 0.05 in walk-forward analysis.
